summary: Network Virtualization over Layer 3 (NVO3) networks need a way for edge devices to find each other and spread tenant MAC and IP information. This informational document explains how Ethernet VPN (EVPN) serves as a scalable control plane for that. It also notes that EVPN keeps independence from the underlay IP fabric, without needing multicast state in it.

plainLanguage.summary: Big data centers pretend to have many private networks over one shared one. This explains how EVPN keeps track of who lives where.

subtitle: A control plane for managing virtualized networks at scale

tldr.problem: Data center networks need a way for edge devices to discover each other and share location information about virtual machines and services across virtualized networks, without relying on inefficient flooding or complex multicast setup in the underlying network.
tldr.mechanism: EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) provides a BGP-based control plane that automatically discovers network edges, distributes MAC and IP information through routes, and enables advanced features like rapid virtual machine mobility and redundancy.
tldr.outcome: NVO3 networks can now scale efficiently without multicast, support complex features like failover and load balancing, and interconnect data centers while maintaining independence from the underlying IP network.

today: RFC 9469 is an Informational document explaining how to apply EVPN to NVO3 networks. EVPN is widely deployed in data centers and is an Internet Standard (RFC 7432). The document reflects current best practices as of September 2023.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
In modern data centers, network virtualization allows many independent virtual networks to run on shared physical infrastructure. Network Virtualization Edge (NVE) devices sit at the edges and encapsulate tenant traffic into tunnels across the shared underlay network. EVPN provides a unified control plane so NVEs can automatically discover each other, learn which MAC and IP addresses are where, and coordinate advanced features like virtual machine migration and redundancy.

Rather than each NVE statically knowing about all other NVEs, or flooding packets to discover neighbors, EVPN uses BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) to advertise reachability and location information. This eliminates the need for Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) in the underlay network, which simplifies deployment and removes state explosion in large data centers.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of asking every neighbor 'Do you know Alice?' every time, the apartment building posts a bulletin board saying 'Alice lives here now', and everyone reads it.

sections.title: How NVO3 Networks Work
sections.content:
In an NVO3 network, tenant systems (virtual machines or physical servers) connect to broadcast domains through Network Virtualization Edges. Each broadcast domain is a virtual Layer 2 network corresponding to a tenant subnet. When a tenant system sends traffic to another system in the same broadcast domain, the ingress NVE encapsulates it (wrapping it in a tunnel header) and sends it across the underlay network to the egress NVE, which unwraps and forwards it locally.

The core challenge is that NVEs must know the tunnel destination IP address and Virtual Network Identifier (VNI) for each destination MAC address. Without a control plane, operators would manually configure this, or NVEs would flood every unknown destination to all other NVEs and learn from the responses. Both approaches are inefficient at scale.
sections.plainLanguage: When a virtual machine sends a message to another, the edge device wraps it in a special envelope with the destination address written on top, and a postman (the underlay network) delivers it. The problem is figuring out what address to write.

sections.title: EVPN Control Plane in Action
sections.content:
EVPN uses BGP multiprotocol extensions to advertise several types of routes. The most important for NVO3 are MAC/IP Advertisement routes (RT-2), which announce that a particular MAC address and optional IP address are reachable via a specific NVE with a specific VNI. When NVE1 learns (from the cloud management system or from data plane learning) that MAC1 with IP1 is attached locally, it advertises a MAC/IP Advertisement route carrying this information.

Remote NVEs receive this route and install the MAC-to-NVE mapping in their bridge tables. When a local tenant system sends a frame destined to MAC1, the ingress NVE looks it up and finds the associated NVE address and VNI, then encapsulates and sends the frame accordingly. EVPN also handles Inclusive Multicast Ethernet Tag routes (RT-3) to set up flooding trees for broadcast and unknown unicast traffic, and uses Ethernet Segment routes (RT-1 and RT-4) for multihoming scenarios where a tenant system connects to multiple NVEs.
sections.plainLanguage: When the building's office opens each morning, it broadcasts 'Alice is at desk 42, Bob at desk 43, Carol at desk 44'. When someone needs to send Alice a message, they look up the board and send it to desk 42.

sections.title: Advanced Capabilities
sections.content:
EVPN enables sophisticated network features critical for data centers. Virtual Machine Mobility means a VM can migrate between NVEs without disrupting traffic: when the VM moves, a new MAC/IP Advertisement route with a higher sequence number updates all remote NVEs instantly. MAC Protection marks certain MACs (like static servers) as sticky so they cannot be inadvertently overwritten. Loop Protection detects duplicate MACs and blocks them to prevent broadcast storms.

Proxy ARP/ND suppresses Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) and Neighbor Discovery floods by having NVEs respond to ARP/ND queries on behalf of known hosts, dramatically reducing broadcast traffic. Multihoming allows a tenant system to connect to multiple NVEs: EVPN uses Designated Forwarder election to determine which NVE handles incoming broadcast traffic (preventing duplication) while allowing all NVEs to forward known unicast traffic for load balancing.

For Layer 3 services, Integrated Routing and Bridging (IRB) connects broadcast domains to IP routing tables. EVPN can support both asymmetric forwarding (where all NVEs know all tenant subnets) and symmetric forwarding (where NVEs advertise IP prefixes to each other). Data Center Interconnect functionality extends these services across Wide Area Networks by working with MPLS or other tunnel types, allowing seamless cross-site tenant connectivity.
sections.plainLanguage: The system can instantly move someone to a different desk, let any desk claim to have the answer to mail questions to avoid congestion, stop someone from pretending to be someone else, or connect to another office building across town.

sections.title: Why EVPN Wins for NVO3
sections.content:
The key advantage of EVPN is that it replaces both the static configuration problem and the flooding problem with a scalable, dynamic control plane. Unlike static approaches, EVPN automatically discovers and adapts to topology changes. Unlike flooding approaches, it does not require multicast in the underlay network, eliminating state explosion and convergence delays. EVPN routes are BGP routes, so they benefit from existing BGP infrastructure, authentication mechanisms, and operational expertise.

EVPN is vendor-agnostic and standards-based (RFC 7432 and extensions), allowing multi-vendor deployments. It gracefully handles both Layer 2 and Layer 3 connectivity requirements and integrates advanced features without protocol changes. Operators can fine-tune and optimize deployments through route targets and other BGP knobs familiar to them. The RFC notes that no new EVPN procedures are introduced; instead, this document describes how existing EVPN mechanisms apply to NVO3 networks.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of hand-writing address books or asking everyone every minute, the building uses a smart system that learns instantly and tells everyone automatically. It's like a text message group for the whole network.
